subject: EdgeCorp POC: header propagation causing session affinity loss — temporary routing policy request
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Singh <nora.singh@edgecorp.ai>, EdgeCorp POC Team <poc@edgecorp.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: EdgeCorp POC: header propagation causing session affinity loss — temporary routing policy request

Nora / EdgeCorp team,

Quick summary: during yesterday's POC run we saw your client (mobile app) occasionally drop session affinity to the same model instance when the client adds a proprietary X-EC-Session header. That header is stripped by an intermediate proxy in our routing path, which causes a burst of requests to be routed to a different variant and breaks your streaming session. Attached: a HAR excerpt and a condensed session trace (session-trace-20260512.txt) showing the correlation between header loss and request routing changes.

As the customer is on a tight demo schedule next week, can we request a temporary routing policy that:
- treats requests from edgecorp IP ranges as "sticky" for 5 minutes (session affinity by client_id),
- or alternatively, a header-preserve passthrough for X-EC-Session for the EdgeCorp demo route.

Concrete asks:
1) Platform/runtime: can you approve a short-lived policy (7 days) scoped to the EdgeCorp demo route so Nora's team can complete their end-to-end flows?
2) Sales/CS: if we do an exemption, what do we need from legal/compliance? (I can surface the limited IP range + duration.)

I'm looping Logan and Karthik for engineering feasibility and a suggested rollback/playbook. We can also stand up a 30-min sync today if useful.

Attachments: edgecorp-har.log (excerpt), session-trace-20260512.txt, edgecorp-poc-mobility-screenshot.png

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Nora Singh <nora.singh@edgecorp.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-12T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeCorp POC: header propagation causing session affinity loss — temporary routing policy request

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the quick analysis and the trace.

A couple clarifications from our side:
- The X-EC-Session header is added by our mobile SDK when users resume in-flight prompts; we rely on it to resume streaming across flaky mobile networks.
- We can provide the CID/IP ranges for our demo kiosk fleet today.

We'd prefer the header-preserve passthrough if that's lower risk than IP-based sticky routing. Demo window is Tue/Wed next week — ideally policy in place by Monday morning.

Let me know if a short runbook or e2e test harness would help validate.

— Nora
Nora Singh
EdgeCorp, Platform Integrations

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Singh <nora.singh@edgecorp.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-12T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeCorp POC: header propagation causing session affinity loss — temporary routing policy request

Kimberly / Nora / team — thanks for the clear repro. Quick notes from the runtime side after a first look:

- The routing layer currently normalizes and removes non-whitelisted headers for security. X-EC-Session is not on the whitelist, so it gets stripped at the LB/edge which explains the observed behavior.
- Two viable short-term options:
  1) Header whitelist and passthrough for X-EC-Session on the EdgeCorp route (low impact scope, but requires a policy change and a rollout to the edge fleet).
  2) Sticky routing by client_id/IP (we can scope to EdgeCorp demo IP ranges), which avoids header changes but pins requests to the same backend and can increase utilization variance.

Trade-offs: header passthrough preserves your semantics but requires us to carefully validate we aren't exposing custom headers to downstream infra. Sticky routing is simpler but may cause hot-shard effects for your demo traffic.

Operational ask: if we go header passthrough, we'll need a 1-hour maintenance window to roll the edge rule and a quick integration test (I propose a scripted client that toggles header set/remove to validate). If we go sticky routing instead, we can toggle policy with no maintenance window but will need to monitor per-instance load.

I'll prepare a short rollback plan. If legal/compliance flags header passthrough we should default to sticky routing.

— Logan
Principal Product Engineer — Serving Runtime
logan_wright@redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Singh <nora.singh@edgecorp.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-12T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeCorp POC: header propagation causing session affinity loss — temporary routing policy request

Thanks Logan — that trade-off framing is helpful. To move forward:
- Nora will send the demo IP ranges tonight.
- Marissa: can you check with Legal about header passthrough implications? If Legal pushes back, we will route sticky by IP for the demo.
- Karthik / Logan: please estimate the time to roll each option and confirm the monitoring checks you'd want me to watch during the demo.

If we can get a scoped header whitelist by end-of-day Monday that would be ideal. If not, please get sticky routing toggled before Monday morning. We have an internal exec demo scheduled Tue 10am PST that EdgeCorp is running as part of a co-demo.

Thanks,
Kimberly

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Singh <nora.singh@edgecorp.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-13T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeCorp POC: header propagation causing session affinity loss — temporary routing policy request

Team — quick feasibility / plan:

Header passthrough (preferred by customer):
- Implementation: add X-EC-Session to edge whitelist + small validation hook before the LB forwards to internal routing.
- Time: ~3 hours to implement + 1 hour canary (we'll deploy to a single edge PoP), then 1 hour to roll globally if canary looks good.
- Risks: need Legal sign-off for propagating custom headers; minimal runtime CPU cost.

Sticky routing by IP:
- Implementation: create a scoped policy keyed by src IP/route map, TTL=5 minutes for affinity.
- Time: ~45 minutes to configure + immediate toggle.
- Risks: potential per-instance load spikes; needs monitoring guardrails (per-instance CPU + token rates).

Rollback/playbook (brief):
1) If we see increased 5xx or CPU>80% on any instance in the next 10 minutes of demo, toggle policy off -> rollback to default.
2) If session resume fails at scale, revert header whitelist and fall back to sticky routing.

I'll schedule the canary for Mon 8:00am PST if Legal signs off. Otherwise I'll put the sticky routing toggle in place Mon 6:00am PST.

Karthik
Staff Engineer — Serving Orchestration
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Singh <nora.singh@edgecorp.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-13T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeCorp POC: header propagation causing session affinity loss — temporary routing policy request

All — I spoke with Legal. Header passthrough for X-EC-Session is allowed for scoped demos provided:
- We only whitelist that single header for the EdgeCorp demo route,
- The scope is timeboxed to 7 days, and
- EdgeCorp signs a one-page security acknowledgement (I can send the template).

Nora — please sign/return the acknowledgement and send the IP ranges. Once I have both, Karthik: you can proceed with the Monday 8am canary for header passthrough. Logan: please provide the short integration test script so EdgeCorp can validate during the canary.

I'll track exec comms and confirm once DocuSign is out.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Engineering
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
